newsitem.title: HONG KONG: COSCO Pac down, news on ports discounted.
newsitem.headline: COSCO Pac down, news on ports discounted.

text.p: COSCO Pacific Ltd's purchase of port terminals in China was positive for the company but the news was swiftly discounted by the market as sentiment was hurt by its HK$1.2 billion share issue, analysts said on Tuesday.

"The size of the acquisition is relatively small and will have limited profit contribution in the next two years, and this (share issue) will cause a slight earnings dilution," said an analyst at MeesPierson Securities.
COSCO Pacific shares closed HK$0.40 down at HK$10.10 on Tuesday after briefly hitting a high of HK$10.75 in early trade.
"It's profit-taking since the purchases came with a surprise and there is no major good news seen from the company in the pipeline," said Connie Lee, an analyst at Dharmala Securities.

Brokers said the stock was seen under pressure after the company said it would raise HK$1.2 billion in a new share issue to parent COSCO (Hong Kong) Group Ltd, which will place an equal amount of existing shares with international investors.
The placement will fund the terminal deal and further, unspecified expansion.
The China-backed container leasing and terminal operating firm said on Monday it would pay HK$455 million to buy stakes in four Chinese ports from its parent.

"The purchases were largely signalled by the management," said Philip Tulk, an analyst at DBS Securities. "Thus everyone expected there are assets being injected and I think the discount was a bit stronger than expected."
But the MeesPierson analyst said sentiment was dampened by the large-scale share placement, which raised more money than the company would need for the Chinese ports.
"It's not good strategy to raise money and let it sit," he said.
COSCO Pacific said the proceeds from the issue would also be used for its China terminals and container manufacturing plants.
The company further allocated HK$494 million of the proceeds to buy port terminals in the Asia-Pacific region, but gave no details about location or timing.

Analysts generally agreed buying terminals in China and the region was a vertical integration strategy that should benefit the company, especially given the strong support of its ultimate parent, China Ocean Shipping (Group) Co (COSCO Beijing).
COSCO Beijing is China's largest shipping group.
"Certainly it makes a lot of sense and they mentioned before that they aim to become a regional transporter," said Alan Kasket, an investment analyst of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Analysts also said the Chinese port stakes purchased at a 10-times price-earnings multiple was relatively cheap.
"The quality of the assets looks very good, especially at Yantian and Shanghai," Tulk said.
COSCO Pacific said the purchase price represented a 31 percent discount to the stakes' net asset value of HK$655 million and 10 times their 1996 net earnings of HK$45.4 million.
But analysts said COSCO Pacific shares traded at a projected 1997 price-earnings multiple of more than 25 times looks a bit expensive.
-- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6369
